Talampaya is often visited together with Ischigualasto on journeys exploring Argentina's ancient natural landscapes. The park is known for its geological and paleontological heritage. Inside the canyon, stone walls stand alongside scattered patches of vegetation.

## Tapachula — a cultural center of Mexico!

## Tapachula — a blend of cultures!

This is the capital of the state of Chiapas and is located near Tacaná Volcano. Over the years, the city has been settled by immigrants from China, Germany, Japan, and Spain. The mix of cultures is reflected in Tapachula's architecture, restaurants, and festivals. Tapachula is also one of Mexico's wealthiest and most educated cities.

On Taquile Island in Lake Titicaca, textile art remains part of everyday life in the local community. Handcraft techniques are passed down through generations, and patterns reflect the cultural beliefs of the islanders. Learning about weaving offers a way to see the island through daily work and the objects made by its artisans.

The island has walking trails, old agricultural terraces, and views across the lake. Trips here begin with a boat journey from Puno. Taquile is distinguished by its combination of waterside scenery and living craft traditions: walking across the island and meeting artisans offer different perspectives on the same place.

American crocodiles can be observed on the Tárcoles River on Costa Rica's Pacific side. The animals live in the river's lower reaches, while the banks and channels provide views of the natural surroundings of this stretch of coastline. Various bird species, including macaws, also inhabit the area.

Boat routes follow the river toward its mouth and along the Guacalillo Canal. From the water, visitors can see the banks, vegetation, and wildlife habitats. A visit to Tárcoles often complements a journey along the central Pacific coast before relaxing in the Quepos area and exploring Manuel Antonio.
